views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Enter the imminent early-October talks from a posture of measured de-escalation — keep the goodwill gestures already made (16-category exemption, soybean/pork exemption, resumed farm purchases) but do not pre-commit to broad structural concessions before the US matches with a real tariff rollback. Continue negotiating toward a limited interim deal while holding firm on red lines (Huawei entity-list treatment, no surrender of Made in China 2025 autonomy).

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high for China, not existential. The dispute is already biting the real economy: official manufacturing PMI has been below 50 for four straight months (49.7 July, 49.5 August), industrial production growth fell to 4.8% in July (lowest since Feb 2002), PPI turned negative for the first time in three years, and US-bound exports fell 6.5% in July (timeline + SCMP/Forbes). By Sept 1, List 4A hit 15% (~$110–125B) and China's own $75B retaliation took effect, with a further $250B hike to 30% (Oct 15) and List 4B (Dec 15) still looming — meaning near-total tariff coverage on Chinese exports plus CNY breaking 7 and a US currency-manipulator designation. That justifies a clearly positive threat reading (~+0.5, 'major export sectors hit, FX pressure'). The action stance is de-escalatory rather than escalatory because China is under real economic strain (manufacturing contraction, weak external demand) and both sides are already signaling a truce: Trump delayed the Oct 1 hike to Oct 15 as a 'goodwill gesture,' and Beijing has matched with exemptions and resumed soybean buying (Reuters/Politico). Escalating further would risk the Oct 15 hike and deepen domestic pain (also amid swine-fever-driven food inflation and Hong Kong unrest); full concession would sacrifice red lines for no confirmed rollback. Hence hold the current posture and negotiate toward a limited deal (~+0.1).
key_factors: Official manufacturing PMI in contraction for 4 straight months (49.7 July, 49.5 August)
Industrial production +4.8% July, lowest since 2002; PPI turned negative; US-bound exports -6.5% July
Near-total US tariff coverage: List 4A 15% (Sept 1), $250B hike to 30% (Oct 15), List 4B (Dec 15); China retaliation on $75B
CNY broke 7 and US designated China a currency manipulator (Aug 5)
Mutual goodwill: Trump delayed Oct 1 hike to Oct 15; China exempted 16 categories then soybeans/pork and resumed farm purchases
Huawei on US Entity List threatens tech supply chain / tech autonomy goal

sources_cited.excerpt: China announces retaliation on ~$75B of US goods; Trump orders US companies to look at alternatives and directs 5-point List 4 hike.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator.
Chinese state media reports soybeans, pork and other farm goods excluded from additional retaliatory tariffs (goodwill signal ahead of talks).
Manufacturing PMI 49.5 in August, fourth consecutive month of contraction; industrial production +4.8% July, lowest since Feb 2002; Q2 GDP 6.2% lowest on record.
US-bound exports fell 6.5% in July; imports from US fell 19.1%; PPI turned negative (-0.3%) for first time in three years.
China exempts soybeans/pork from additional tariffs and resumes purchases; Trump delayed Oct 1 hike to Oct 15 as goodwill gesture; talks set for early October.
